items.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997
items.q: I used to stay up until twelve o’clock midnight to listen to Cab Calloway. I liked the way he sang, you know, he was a shouter. But the band was excellent.

ctx.x: Who were you listening to on the records at that time?

Duke Ellington and oh I used to stay up until twelve o’clock midnight to listen to Cab Calloway. I liked the way he sang, you know, he was a shouter. But the band was excellent. The band was excellent. From the Cotton Club up in Harlem. And Duke Ellington of course we would listen to. It seemed at the time that the most popular bands were the colored bands for some reason or other. The white bands weren’t that popular, outside of Paul Whiteman we’ll say, who was a big name anyway, and Ben Bernie who was on the…
They were more on the sweet side of music rather than the jazz?
